title: Declare multiple variables on one line
description: Write a function `assign_three(values)` that takes a 3-item sequence and returns it unpacked into a tuple `(a, b, c)`, using multiple assignment on one line (`a, b, c = values`) rather than indexing.
hints: Idea to consider: multiple assignment - several names on the left of one =

Python lets you put several names on the left of a single = sign, one per element of whatever's on the right - a shortcut for assigning to each name one at a time with values[0], values[1], values[2].
Unpack values into three names with one assignment statement, then return those three names as a tuple.
expected_behavior: Returns the three values unpacked into a tuple.
explanation: Multiple assignment works with any sequence of the matching length on the right-hand side - it's not specific to literal tuples like a, b, c = 1, 2, 3.
